key_insight: Combining polynomial reduced-order models with quantum transport preserves nonlinear flow dynamics while making per-step rotation counts scale polylogarithmically with grid cells per coordinate at fixed model dimension and drift degree.
engineering_relevance: Reduced-model polynomial degree becomes a design variable for balancing flow-model accuracy against early fault-tolerant quantum hardware costs.
method: Fit polynomial reduced-order models using sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics.
Implement Koopman–von Neumann transport with Walsh-synthesized quantum circuits.
Estimate end-to-end costs using surface-code resource models.
evidence_signal: For a cylinder wake approaching saturation, the study estimates 1.62 hours on about 560,000 physical qubits for 1% relative RMS field error against the radial model, and demonstrates nonlinear radial transport on IBM hardware with reference-circuit noise mitigation.
watch_item: The fault-tolerant runtimes are estimates, with three-coordinate wake cases spanning hours to weeks; the reported 1% error is measured against a reduced radial model.
paper_title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
